navigation: Main laboratory; fixed left/right routes from spawn are not established.
Free movement must be permitted and not locked by a tutorial or experiment.
Move with W/A/S/D. Hold the right mouse button and move the mouse to look around. E/Q move up/down in the desktop controller; LeftShift accelerates.
Input assets include left-thumbstick locomotion; the enabled headset locomotion setup requires device verification.
Player position and viewing direction change.
Arrival requires runtime position evidence, not conversation alone.
CameraTryMove is enabled and Move is disabled in the audited main scene. Desktop debug vertical movement is not physical walking.
teleport: Accessible surfaces in the main laboratory.
Movement must be unlocked and the target must pass ray, slope, and reachability checks.
The controller maps G to movement toward the pointed reachable ground.
Roaming/AutoMove maps to gripButton, but Move is disabled in the main scene; this is not confirmed available XR guidance.
Movement toward the target may be constrained by collision and reachability.
Verify a change in runtime position.
The XR route needs verification. Do not promise that every selected point is reachable or recommend an action absent from the live allowlist.
sample_pick: Four dishes: red beside the ultrasonic cleaner, green beside the centrifuge, blue/yellow on the workbench in front of the microscope.
Enter specimen range and register it as the current interactable. SNOM/assembly interactions take priority; removal takes priority if a specimen is already placed.
Approach an interactable specimen and left-click to pick it up.
Approach an interactable specimen and press the right-hand trigger.
The runtime specimen and inventory texture update.
HasSampleOnHand, CurrentSampleTexture, and SampleChanged provide state evidence; use the current supplied snapshot.
Another specimen can be selected. No generic discard key is confirmed.
A ray hit alone does not establish registration. The old R-to-pickup instruction is incorrect.
sample_place_observe: Place a specimen and enter observation
The interactive microscope in the main laboratory, within its trigger range.
Hold an ObserveObjects specimen and satisfy isNear and MicroUI.setTrue.
Press Z to place the specimen. When already placed, press Z to advance observation viewpoints until Observing.
Press the left-hand trigger to place, then use the same input to advance observation viewpoints.
The specimen appears on the stage and the viewpoint enters observation.
In Observing, Z or Esc exits on desktop; the left-hand trigger exits in XR.
Placement and pointer/viewpoint advancement are separate. A single press need not complete the entire sequence.
sample_remove: Within interaction range of the microscope.
Leave internal observation first; a specimen must be on the stage.
Left-click within microscope interaction range to remove the specimen.
Press the right-hand trigger to remove the specimen.
The specimen moves from the microscope back to the player.
Check HasPlacedSample changes, not just the inventory icon.
The same input also handles component/SNOM selection; use the appropriate current mode.
illumination: The interactive microscope and observation interface.
Light toggling requires proximity and available external interaction.
Press B in external interaction mode to toggle the light. Hold X and use up/down arrows for illumination adjustment.
Use the right-hand secondaryButton to toggle the light externally. Hold the left-hand primaryButton and move the right thumbstick up/down to adjust illumination.
The illustrative light/aperture and observation display change.
Use reported light state such as GetLight; a key press alone does not establish the resulting state.
Q is desktop downward movement, not the old light shortcut. LightSwitch is not bound inside Observing.
objective_switch: The interactive microscope or internal observation view.
Microscope interaction must be available; wait for turret rotation to finish.
Press the right-hand primaryButton to switch objectives.
The objective turret or displayed magnification changes.
A current objective/camera state report is needed to identify the actual setting.
R means Replay in the SNOM tour. Magnification is not synonymous with NA.
focus: Press Tab to switch coarse/fine mode. Hold X and use left/right arrows to focus.
Press the right thumbstick to switch coarse/fine mode. Hold the left-hand primaryButton and move the right thumbstick left/right to focus.
Compare clarity and coarse/fine adjustment feedback.
Actual focus parameters and mode require a corresponding runtime report.
Use Z/Esc on desktop or the left-hand trigger in XR to leave observation.
Use the current input chain, not obsolete M/B/N shortcuts. Display feedback is not calibrated imaging.
assembly: Enter, expand, and restore the assembly
The whole microscope assembly model in the main scene.
No tutorial, experiment transition, or independent experiment may lock the mode.
Left-click the whole assembly for PreAssembly, then click again for SuperAssembly and wait for expansion.
Point the right-hand ray at the assembly and press the trigger for PreAssembly; repeat for SuperAssembly.
The intact model becomes an exploded structure.
CurrentMode and ModelExploder.IsExploded/IsAnimating describe this state.
Leave component selection first. Select outside the model to return SuperAssembly to PreAssembly, then outside again for Normal.
Inputs are handled by stage. A single blank-area click does not exit every level.
parts: The expanded microscope components in SuperAssembly.
Expansion must finish and no other experiment may lock selection.
Left-click a component and read its right-hand panel. Select outside the panel/component to leave the selection.
Use the right-hand ray and trigger to select a component; select outside its UI/component to leave.
Configured names: Objective Lens, Upper Optical Assembly, Stage Position Control, Optical Breadboard, Focus Adjustment.
Use IsSelectionActive and current selectedPart/partDescription context.
After leaving selection, follow the assembly return sequence.
Internal optics of Upper Optical Assembly are not individually confirmed. Do not call it a dichroic mirror or pinhole. The last three listed components have no independent experiment button.
na_experiment: Upper Optical Assembly in the expanded model; internal node AboveMirror.
Complete assembly expansion and select Upper Optical Assembly.
Select Start Numerical Aperture Experiment, wait, then drag the NA slider and compare angles, cone, and approximate magnification.
Use the UI ray for the same button and slider. A fallback reads the x axis of Roaming/ChangeFocusOrChangeLIght, usually with the left primary modifier; verify on the actual device.
NA ranges from 0.03 to 0.95; theta, full angle, and cone change.
IsExperimentActive, IsTransitioning, CurrentNA, and CaptureTeachingState are implemented.
Select Exit to return to the component; then use the component/assembly exit sequence.
NA=n sin(theta). Magnification interpolates reference settings; brightness, clarity, and depth feedback are teaching mappings.
spatial_frequency: Objective Lens in the expanded model; internal node ObjectLen.
Expand and select Objective Lens. Select a specimen first to see specimen-derived spectra.
Select Start Spatial Frequency Experiment and wait. High/Middle/Low are 250/125/62.5 lines/mm. Select White Light/Laser Excitation; hold specimen and illumination fixed for a carrier-only comparison.
Use the right-hand UI ray for the same entry, frequency, and illumination controls.
Compare grating, diffraction spacing, specimen spectrum, sidebands, and multi-orientation support.
IsExperimentActive, CaptureTeachingState, and SampleChanged support state collection.
Select Exit to return to the component view.
Without a specimen, derived spectrum panels are empty. This is not confocal pinhole simulation or complete SIM image reconstruction.
snom_entry: Main-scene model TDs_edited_UnityVeryLowPoly; use runtime geometry for direction.
Approach SNOM; its runtime controller must find the model and create the entry.
Click the SNOM target to show its entry, then select Begin Operation.
Use the right-hand ray and trigger for the SNOM target, then select Begin Operation.
Read the current workflow phase and stage from the controller snapshot.
Select Exit, or Esc on desktop when available.
RuntimeBootstrap creates this module dynamically. Absence of a directly attached scene script does not mean the feature is absent.
snom_probe: Select Fine/Standard/Robust or press 1/2/3. Select Install Selected Probe or press E, then wait.
Use the UI ray to select a probe card and Install Selected Probe.
The preview moves to its mount; Start System appears after installation.
ReadyToStart establishes completion of installation; the install click alone does not.
Select Exit or use desktop Esc when available.
3x/2x/1x are relative-detail teaching labels, not objective magnifications. The meshes are not three calibrated physical probes.
snom_start: Start SNOM and observe its principles
Probe installation must finish and Start System must be available.
Select Start System or press Space.
Select Start System with the UI ray.
Eight automatic stages cover THz generation, beam steering, AFM feedback, near-field coupling, scattering/background, demodulation, raster scan, and results/local spectrum.
Use the current stage and supplied playback state; do not invent scan progress.
Select Exit or use desktop Esc when available.
Installing and starting are player actions; the eight subsequent stages explain internal processes rather than eight additional instrument operations.
snom_controls: Start the system to enter the principle tour.

Previous/Next or left/right arrows change stage. Play/pause or Space controls playback; Replay or R repeats a stage. Components opens component explanations. Use Change Probe only when that button is displayed.
Use the UI ray for currently visible Previous, Next, play/pause, Replay, and Components controls.
Animations, diagrams, and text change with the selected stage/component.
Use current stage, selection, and playback state.
Select Exit or use desktop Esc when available.
Separate Raw/2Omega/3Omega buttons are not confirmed despite earlier design proposals. Displayed results are synthetic.
forced_tutorial: Meet the trigger, sequence, specimen, and state prerequisites.
Perform the input shown for the current step; not every step is a Space confirmation.
Perform the requested controller action; combinations may require holding a modifier.
Matching input/events advance a step; some presentation steps advance automatically.
Use tutorial completion events and trigger state, not dialog claims.
Complete the tutorial sequence; no universal skip control is confirmed.
The tutorial may lock movement, assembly, or global input; suspend idle reminders while blocked.
optional_tutorial: Panel registered as Interactor.currentTutorial; the audited main-scene direct reference is null.
Confirm a runtime Tutorial instance registers currentTutorial.
Code maps Y to open, arrows/WASD to navigation, and Space/Enter to confirm when the menu is active.
Global/OpenTutorial maps to left secondaryButton; right thumbstick navigates and right primaryButton confirms.
A correctly registered instance displays tutorial lists or observation tutorials.
The direct main-scene attachment is not established; do not promise availability.
This is not the assistant wake control. Old H documentation is not the current mapping. Missing registration risks null references.
stage_translation: ScreenMove needs an enabled instance on a target with a specimen child.
Verify the actual component instance and enabled state.
Code reads Horizontal/Vertical (WASD/arrows), but current scene availability is not confirmed.
The specimen translates in its local XY plane.
No direct main-scene reference was established; a prefab instance may exist. A script alone does not authorize operating instructions.
filter_prototype: PCDesktop scripts and light-path assets; no complete entry is confirmed.
Actual UI, drag/drop, and slot binding need verification.
Filter, DichroicMirror, Slot, and light-line component code exists.

confocal_background: Knowledge explanation, related to microscope structure, NA, and spatial frequency; no full confocal interaction workflow.
Explain excitation, collection, rejection of defocus by a pinhole, and scanning as concepts.
There is no executable completion condition.
Do not instruct pinhole adjustment, Z-stack acquisition, detector control, or real scanning parameters. NA/spectrum activities are not confocal optical sectioning.
legacy_tutor: Removed from NA and spatial-frequency experiments.
Old panels and fixed questions are unavailable; the aurora assistant remains.
Dedicated source, assets, editor menus, and the old /tutor route were removed.
Historical entry retained only to prevent recommendations of the removed feature.
aurora_assistant: Upper-left of the main laboratory; runtime Local Aurora Assistant uses a camera-following world-space Canvas in XR.
The main scene must run with LocalAssistantSettings.assistantEnabled=true. Verify display and input on the target device.
Press H or select the orb for a local greeting; H is ignored while editing input. Select Ask a question, enter a question or choose a topic, then Send. Voice Input records a draft for confirmation.
Select the orb and controls with the existing XR UI ray; no additional experiment-controller shortcut is introduced.

Local greetings, idle reminders, English knowledge chat, confirmed speech drafts, current-state instructions, and location markers are implemented. Only submitted chat/transcription uses external services.
Runtime message, idle, guidance, and navigation state provide implementation evidence; device testing must be reported separately.
Close the message, or select Snooze 5 min to pause idle reminders; manual activation remains available.

Backend configuration is required for real model/voice use. Actions guide the learner and do not execute instrument controls. Historical stage-two limitations have been superseded by current state/navigation/voice code.
